question: A pilot has worked well, and the team wants the new way of working to survive the departure of the person who created it. Which sequence of steps is correct?
options: A) Correct the instructions wherever they got stuck; have a second person run the work from those instructions alone; capture the working instructions in one shared place; write down what a good result looks like.

B) Write down what a good result looks like; capture the working instructions in one shared place; have a second person run the work from those instructions alone; correct the instructions wherever they got stuck.

C) Capture the working instructions in one shared place; correct the instructions wherever they got stuck; write down what a good result looks like; have a second person run the work from those instructions alone.

D) Have a second person run the work from those instructions alone; write down what a good result looks like; correct the instructions wherever they got stuck; capture the working instructions in one shared place.
correct_answers: B) Write down what a good result looks like; capture the working instructions in one shared place; have a second person run the work from those instructions alone; correct the instructions wherever they got stuck.
explanations: This begins by correcting instructions that do not yet exist in a shared place and ends by defining the standard, so every earlier step was taken without knowing what success meant.

Correct. The quality standard has to exist before anyone can tell whether a handover succeeded, the instructions must be captured somewhere shared to be handed over at all, a second person running from them alone is the real test, and their sticking points show precisely what to correct.
Correcting the instructions before anyone has tried to follow them means correcting imagined problems, and the standard for a good result is written after the corrections it should have guided.
The second person cannot run the work from instructions that have not yet been captured, and writing down what good looks like after the test leaves them no way to judge their own output.
